classification.difficultyReason: Express two changing perpendicular distances in terms of time and combine them using Pythagoras to derive a distance model.

content.prompt:
Joel is 700 km north of a town, travelling towards it at an average speed of $75\text{ km h}^{-1}$.

Nick is 680 km east of the town, travelling towards it at $80\text{ km h}^{-1}$.

Show that, after $t$ hours, the distance between Joel and Nick is
$$d=\sqrt{952\,400-213\,800t+12\,025t^2}.$$

spec.description: Joel lies vertically north of Town and Nick horizontally east of Town. The joining diagonal completes the right triangle. Both initial distance labels and the right-angle marker are retained.
spec.mathematics: The initial perpendicular distances from Town are 700 km and 680 km.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question diagram containing initial givens only.

answer.worked:
After $t$ hours, Joel has travelled $75t$ km and is $700-75t$ km from the town. Nick has travelled $80t$ km and is $680-80t$ km from the town.

By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}d^2&=(700-75t)^2+(680-80t)^2\\d^2&=490\,000-105\,000t+5625t^2+462\,400-108\,800t+6400t^2\\d^2&=952\,400-213\,800t+12\,025t^2\\d&=\sqrt{952\,400-213\,800t+12\,025t^2}\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
The positive square root gives the distance.
